mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds rate rises by at least 0.25 percentage points over the next month, investors anticipate tighter credit conditions, which reduces the discount rate applied to future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the following 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by ≥ 0.25pp from current value within 1 month
failure_condition: Over a 12-month walk-forward, the 5-day forward returns do not deviate from the pre-trigger mean by more than one standard deviation during active tightening periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in CPIAUCSL by at least 0.5% over two consecutive months signals a disinflationary trend, prompting investors to price in lower future inflation and thereby drive S&P 500 forward returns positively over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL decreases by ≥ 0.5% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: In regimes satisfying the trigger, the 60-day forward return is not statistically different from the prior 60-day average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in PAYEMS (labor market additions) of at least 10% month-over-month, followed by a stabilization in UNRATE, predicts a temporary boost in consumer and business confidence, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by ≥ 10% MoM and UNRATE remains below pre-increase level for the following month
regime_hint: expansionary labor market with cooling wage pressures
failure_condition: During the specified window, the 20-day forward return is negative and statistically significant (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When GDPC1 (real private demand) grows faster than GDP deflator (CPIAUCSL) by at least 2% quarter-over-quarter, it indicates stronger real demand, which supports higher corporate earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth rate exceeds CPIAUCSL growth rate by ≥ 2% QoQ
failure_condition: In regimes satisfying the trigger, the 60-day forward return is flat or negative with a p-value > 0.05 in a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in INDPRO (industrial production) by at least 5% month-over-month, without a parallel decline in HOUST (housing starts), suggests supply-side weakness that raises uncertainty and depresses S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by ≥ 5% MoM while HOUST does not decline over the same period
regime_hint: industrial production contraction absent housing resilience
failure_condition: During such events, the 20-day forward return is not statistically different from the prior 20-day average (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 3.5% for three consecutive months in a deflationary regime, it signals weaker labor market resistance to wage cuts, lowering discount rates and pushing S&P 500 forward returns downward over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 3.5% for three consecutive months and regime_hint indicates deflationary conditions
failure_condition: The 5-day forward return is positive and statistically significant (p < 0.05) during the trigger period.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in RSAFS (reserves as a share of GDP) by at least 0.5 percentage points over three months indicates excess liquidity, which typically supports risk-on sentiment and produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases by ≥ 0.5pp over three consecutive months
failure_condition: During such liquidity expansion, the 20-day forward return is not statistically higher than the 30-day rolling average (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When a combination of falling UNRATE (<3.5%) and rising FEDFUNDS (>4.5%) occurs simultaneously for two consecutive months, it signals conflicting expectations that suppress growth and equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 3.5% and FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for two consecutive months
regime_hint: conflicting policy and labor market signals
failure_condition: In this regime, the 60-day forward return is positive and statistically significant (p < 0.05) in at least 40% of such windows over a 5-year sample.
